internet.heading: The Internet
internet.subheading: A short history, and why I love it.
points: 1969: ARPANET sends its first message between two computers.
1991: Tim Berners-Lee publishes the first website.
1996: My first encounter with the Internet. In an Internet café in Dublin.
Today: billions of people, connected in real time.
Why I love it: anyone, anywhere, can build something and put it in front of the world.

studioFi.heading: Studio Fi
points: After leaving OrangeFluid: WordPress, then React, until finding the stack I like.
Building websites in three languages: Irish, English, and German.
Customer-focused, fast response times, and clever solutions.
Giving people a space to control their own corner of the internet — away from rigid WordPress templates.

strengthsWeaknesses.heading: The Strengths and Weaknesses of Studio Fi
strengthsWeaknesses.subheading: A small studio with a personal approach and room to grow.

strengths.title: Personal service
strengths.description: Clients speak directly with me throughout the project.

strengths.title: Fast decisions
strengths.description: There is no large agency process slowing down useful ideas.

strengths.title: Custom websites
strengths.description: Each project is built around the client instead of a rigid WordPress template.

weaknesses.title: Limited capacity
weaknesses.description: As a small studio, there is a limit to how many large projects I can handle at once.

weaknesses.title: Too many roles
weaknesses.description: One person currently carries design, development, communication, and operations.

weaknesses.title: Developing processes
weaknesses.description: Some systems and processes are still being built as Studio Fi grows.

product.heading: The Product
product.subheading: A business-card website is the hook. A custom CRM is the real sell.
product.problem: Small businesses manage everything behind a marketing tool — a website — instead of a system built around how they actually run.
product.insight: WordPress won because it gave people control. We can go further: a website with a backend, built entirely around the client.

pillars.title: Business-card website
pillars.description: A professional front door — the entry point every client expects.

pillars.title: Custom dashboard
pillars.description: A backend that does whatever the client needs, because we build it.

pillars.title: Built-in CRM
pillars.description: Track customers, bookings, and sales in one place.

pillars.title: Run the business, not just market it
pillars.description: Set up seminars, sell clothes, manage clients — all from the same site.

product.closing: Custom websites and CRMs, built for the client, at a price small businesses can actually afford.

academyFiPanel.heading: Academy Fi vs. Studio Fi
academyFiPanel.subheading: Two panels, two jobs — don't mix them up.
academyFiPanel.intro: This app you've been using all day is Academy Fi. It's not where client work happens — it's where your internship gets logged.

pillars.title: Academy Fi
pillars.description: Where you log your internship: departments, assignments, reflections, and feedback.

pillars.title: Studio Fi
pillars.description: Where you log the actual work for Studio Fi: clients, projects, and the custom CRM from the product slide.

academyFiPanel.closing: Same idea, two systems — Studio Fi builds its own tools the same way it builds them for clients.
